Verse Engine — naming glossary#

Definitions are taken from the doc comments and specs they cite: docs/architecture.md, the container format spec (in-repo, for the team), crates/verse-render/src/vg_residency.rs, crates/verse-core/src/wire.rs, crates/verse-core/src/anim.rs, crates/verse-rhi/src/lib.rs, web/playground/caps.js, web/playground/triple-buffer.js. Where a term is used with two meanings in the code, both are listed.

Virtualized geometry#

cluster — The draw unit of virtualized geometry: a meshlet of up to 128 triangles / 256 vertices with its own bounding sphere, own_error, parent_error, quantization AABB, material and payload range (112-byte entry in the .vpk cluster table). Rendered as one fixed 384-vertex instance, degenerate past the real triangle count.

group — The streaming and simplification unit. In the compiler: a set of adjacent clusters simplified together with the group border locked, then re-split into parent clusters. In the file: a contiguous run of child clusters, one byte range, one FNV-1a checksum (32-byte v5 group entry). Residency is group-atomic. A cluster is a child of parent_group (its residency unit) and a parent of own_group (the group that refines it).

DAG cut — The set of clusters drawn in a frame. Cut rule: draw a cluster iff project(own_error) ≤ τ < project(parent_error). Errors grow strictly up the DAG (parent_error > own_error is enforced on read), which keeps a mixed-level cut crack-free. Evaluated per cluster in vg_cull (shaders/vg.wgsl), and on the CPU for the burst plan.

own error / parent error — own_error: object-space error of this cluster versus the source mesh, projected through own_test_sphere (the group that produced it; identical on both sides of a boundary). parent_error: the error of drawing its parents instead, projected through parent_test_sphere; +∞ at roots. τ is the pixel budget.

residency — Which groups are loaded into GPU pool slots right now. Group-atomic and top-down: a group may only be resident when every group holding its parent clusters is resident, because the cut falls back to a parent when a child is absent. The CPU state machine is Residency in vg_residency.rs (pure, headless-tested); gpu.rs owns the buffers. Roots (clusters with no parent_group) are always resident.

closure (requires / enables) — The top-down dependency graph. requires[g] = groups holding g's parent clusters; they must be resident before g loads (Admission::NeedsParent otherwise). enables[g] = the inverse edge: groups that list g in their requires — the eviction guard (g cannot be evicted while a dependent is loaded). Edges are added by link_clusters: a cluster that is both a child of parent_group and a parent of own_group says "own_group requires parent_group". closure_holds() is the debug invariant.

wants — GPU feedback: every drawn cluster that wanted refinement stamps the group it would refine into with the current frame number (wants[g] = last frame g was wanted; 0 = never). plan_from_wants turns stamps within WANT_HORIZON (120 frames) into a fetch plan — absent groups with their missing ancestors first, capped to what can land (free slots + evictable, at most TICK_CAP = 24). A group wanted within EVICT_GRACE (60 frames) is never evicted.

burst plan — Instant refine: burst_plan walks the refinement cut for a camera entirely on the CPU from the directory (every resident cluster entry carries its sphere and error) and returns the unloaded groups the cut needs, ancestors strictly before dependents — one call instead of one GPU round trip per DAG level. With a paged directory the walk stops at the resident prefix and resumes when the next page lands. Related: preload_list, the coarse-first warmup fetched right after the roots (≤ 512 KiB, never more than half the pool).

head / page (.vpk v5) — The head is the byte prefix the runtime opens on: [header 128 B | group table | first n cluster entries], with n = min(cluster_count, 32 768) (~3.7 MB regardless of scene size). It must contain every root entry. The remaining cluster entries are fetched in order as pages — whole, contiguous entries not overrunning cluster_count — and appended with Directory::extend / vg_dir_extend; Admission::NeedsPage gates any group whose children's entries are not paged in yet. v ≤ 4 files (group table after the entries) open on the whole directory as a single head.

Hi-Z — A hierarchical depth pyramid (hiz.wgsl) at a fixed virtual resolution, deliberately independent of render resolution so DRS scale changes cannot misalign it. Used for two-phase occlusion culling of clusters: vg_cull tests against the pyramid in phase 1, the pyramid is rebuilt after the main pass, and a phase-1 → phase-2 re-test queue gives occluded-then-revealed clusters a second chance. ?vghiz=0 disables it for measurement.

probe — Two uses. (1) Environment probe: a 128² cube map of the streamed scene rendered from the walker's position (vg_bake_probe, bake-probe message) that mirror-like materials sample. (2) QA probe: the drawn-cluster readback (visible_stats) that feeds the ~1 Hz culling stats in the HUD.

Rendering#

tier A / B / C / – — Device class. Engine side (verse-rhi Tier): A = WebGPU with max_storage_buffer_binding_size > 128 MiB and max_buffer_size > 256 MiB (full pipeline); B = WebGPU with reduced, mobile-class limits (reduced budgets); C = the WebGL2 build, by construction whatever the hardware (classic meshes, procedural sky, no post chain; streamed scenes open with a CPU-selected cut; no splats). Page side (caps.js detect) reports A/B (WebGPU adapter + OffscreenCanvas; the engine then decides A vs B), C (WebGL2 only), or – (neither: poster + link-out, the engine never boots).

TSR — Temporal super-resolution ("4K Mode", ?temporal=1, embed quality: "4k"). Replaces MSAA with jitter + motion vectors and reconstructs output-resolution detail from a scaled render using a ping-pong history at output resolution. Not available on tier C; depth of field and the stereo (XR) path are not applied in temporal mode.

DRS — Dynamic resolution scaling: a PI controller on the sensed frame time that moves the internal render scale within [0.5, 1.0] to hold the frame budget. ?scale= pins the scale and disables the controller. The thermal predictor (thermal.rs) caps the DRS ceiling when it regresses an upward drift in pixel-normalized cost (sensed_ms / scale²).

Animation (FEAT-8)#

deform block — The per-frame f32 block the sim appends to the snapshot for skinning and morphing: joint palettes (16 words per joint) and morph weights (one word per target), capped at 256 joints' worth. Per-instance pointers (deform_base, morph_base; -1 / MAX = none, bind-pose fallback) address into it.

palette — A skin's joint matrices for one frame: inverse(mesh world) × joint world × inverse bind, so the vertex shader skins in mesh space before applying the model matrix. A rig (wire::pack_rig) carries the rest-pose node hierarchy, clips, skins (joint node indices + inverse bind matrices), per-instance skin index and morph defaults.

Workers and wire#

snapshot / wire — verse-core/src/wire.rs defines the packed f32 formats crossing worker boundaries so both sides compile from one module. The frame snapshot (sim → render, every tick) is [time, view_proj, view, proj, camera_pos, bounds, instance_count, instances × 24 words, light_count, lights, …deform block]; a torn or truncated slot deserializes to None rather than panicking. The scene description (render → main → sim, once per load) packs the node list + bounds; the rig packs animation data beside it.

triple buffer — web/playground/triple-buffer.js: a lock-free, wait-free exchange over a SharedArrayBuffer — three f32 slots in the wire format plus one atomic "latest" word {slot index, dirty bit} in a 64-byte header. The writer publishes with one Atomics.exchange and continues into the slot it got back; the reader swaps its held slot for the latest. Writer and reader can never hold the same slot, so no torn reads and nobody waits. Only exists when the page is cross-origin isolated.

sim worker / render worker — The render worker (render-worker.js) owns the wasm VerseEngine and the OffscreenCanvas: streaming loop, texture streaming, picking, environment swaps, golden capture, frame telemetry; restarted by the main-thread watchdog after 8 s without a message. The sim worker (sim-worker.js) runs the fixed-cadence ECS tick — camera, walk physics, collision against the occupancy grid, animation playback — and publishes snapshots through the triple buffer. Without cross-origin isolation there is no sim worker and the render worker ticks a camera-only fallback world (telemetry mode: "fallback").

Ingest#

ingest job — The unit of the asynchronous compile API. POST /v1/ingest stores the GLB, spawns verse-compile, and answers 202 { job }; GET /v1/ingest/<job> returns { status: "compiling" | "done" | "error", … } plus the compiler's phase (stage) and an estimate while running, and { url, vpkUrl, stats } when done. Job records are kept 2 h after completion (404 afterwards); the compiled ingest/<id>.vpk is retained and served; the uploaded GLB is deleted after compile (unless the scene was published in compatibility mode, where the GLB is the scene). A **scene id** in the embed SDK (data-scene) is this ingest handle: it resolves to ingest/<scene>.vpk on the Verse origin.
